ruling_text_quoted: [retrieve.py:609-615] C-8(ii)/(iii): the population is resolved ONCE here, as a PURE-PYTHON filter over the crystal dicts already in hand (`bm25_search` returns full rows) — never a status predicate on the shared `bm25_search`, and no extra I/O beyond the one bounded aggregate below (DP-3, "the existing bounded aggregate", `count_for_export`; no new public storage method, per FORGE's ruling). [echo, retrieve.py:241-242] `bm25_search` applies no status predicate (shared method, never filtered).
rationale: Letter: the top-up adds no SQL status predicate, no bm25_search parameter, and no new public storage method — every named prohibition holds, and AC-349 independently freezes the shared method's signature and SQL. Spirit: read in situ, all four clauses of the fence sentence share one grammatical subject — how the D3 selectivity POPULATION is resolved (once, pure-Python, over rows already in hand, with count_for_export the only aggregate I/O). The fence pins the LOCUS of status-awareness to the caller so that the shared read path stays status-blind for both consumers (layers/episodic.py:319 untouched either way) and so that exactly one predicate (_is_active, deliberately hoisted at retrieve.py:564-584 for population parity — 'never a second divergent definition') defines 'active'. The caller-side top-up does not defeat that purpose; it is that purpose's forced consequence: barred from pushing the predicate into SQL, the only possible remedy for a status-censored fetch is fetch-wider-and-filter at the caller, using the same status-blind method and the same single predicate. The strongest DENY reading — 'no extra I/O' as a whole-recall bound, making a second same-query call the forbidden predicate-by-loop — is refuted by the recorded corpus itself: D3 (binding) already ruled Option A's backstop calls fence-clean ('existing signature, existing filters, bounded calls'), and a reading under which the fence voids D3 and renders D6's live production defect structurally unfixable is a misreading of the ruling, not the ruling. The population-resolution step the fence actually governs is untouched by the top-up: still resolved once, still pure-Python, still one bounded aggregate — only the set of rows in hand widens, by at most one bounded call per censored-and-dirty fetch.

composition_ruling: RAMZA's head-only choice is UPHELD on the default (all-layers) and single-layer paths — there the head is the only fetch, so head-only and locus-widening coincide and B.4.2 stands verbatim — and OVERRULED as the exclusive rule on Option A's strict-subset path. Normative rule (an open amendment of D3's AC-348 '<=1' clause, composing D3+D6+D7 with the per-fetch shape D1 already authorised for its terminal branch): the top-up widens each fetch that is INDIVIDUALLY censored-and-dirty, at most once per fetch — on the strict-subset path that is the global head (when its post-filtered contribution is dirty and the head censored) and/or each per-layer backstop call (censored at candidate_k and dirty) — never a widen decided by another fetch's signal, which is the K-B13(c) 'property of the fetch' principle applied per fetch, the very ground Kupo cited when judging head-only sound. Head-only is near-inert on the subset path by K-N12's own premise (a wider global head returns mostly excluded-layer rows the post-filter discards, while the starvation locus — a deprecated-censored per-layer backstop call — is never widened), and would ship explain.sparse_topup.fired=true with structurally absent recovery: the F-V3 counter-honesty defect as designed behaviour. Budget: <=1 extra call on default/single-layer (AC-348 unchanged there); <=1+len(target_layers) on strict subsets (AC-348 restated per-path — D1's terminal-branch restatement shape). The censoring signal feeding resolve_sparse_weight remains the head's, recomputed only when the head itself widens; per K-C-N13 the per-fetch raw counts MUST be captured at the call sites (len(sparse_ranking) is NOT the head's raw count on the subset path — W-45 implements the B.3.2 capture, W-44 reads it). What can FAIL on this choice: the NEW mandatory node test_subset_status_topup_recovers_active_hits (K-N12 regime: excluded-layer-dominated censored head, target-layer backstop call deprecated-censored above a planted active target, recall_active_only=True) — RED under head-only, GREEN only with the backstop-locus widen — plus AC-348's per-path spy and AC-356's inertness control. If that discriminating fixture cannot be built, route to S-13 and SUPPRESS the top-up on the strict-subset path explicitly (documented inertness + follow-up filing); never ship the subset-path behaviour unmeasured.

reversal_condition: If W-44 cannot satisfy AC-345/AC-346/AC-348/AC-355/AC-356 plus the new subset-efficacy node within the authorised checklist — i.e. the only green path requires a bm25_search parameter or SQL change, a new storage method, a status predicate in SQL, or an unbounded refetch loop — this ALLOW is void, S-10 fires, and #44 is re-filed rather than half-fixed. Independently: if Config.recall_active_only's default ever flips to False (config.py:333 or the env default at config.py:437), D6's production-defect classification reverts to configuration-gated (D6's own reversal) — the fence verdict itself is unaffected. The composition ruling reverses if the discriminating node shows the backstop-locus widen breaking AC-355 or exceeding the stated budget: the bounded fallback is explicit subset-path suppression, never relaxation of AC-348 or AC-355.
